chunks: From him, from Mu'alla, from Al-Washa, from Abdul-Karim ibn Amr, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'When you see that poverty and need have become abundant, and people are denying each other, then at that time await the Command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I recognize these two – poverty and need – so what is 'people denying each other'?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A man from among you comes to his brother and asks him for his need, and he looks at him with a look unlike the one he used to look with, and speaks to him with a tongue/manner unlike the one he used to speak with.'

key_terms.بِغَيْرِ اللِّسَانِ: With a different tongue/manner (change in speech)
key_terms.بِغَيْرِ الْوَجْهِ: With a different face/look (change in demeanor)

ai.seo_question: What does 'people denying each other' mean in the context of the signs of the end times?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) identifies the deterioration of social etiquette as a critical precursor to the emergence of Gog and Magog, linking economic scarcity to spiritual alienation. This hadith highlights that 'denial' manifests not just in material refusal, but in the loss of familiar warmth and brotherly conduct, signaling a society where interpersonal bonds have frayed under pressure. In Shia eschatology, this social fragmentation is viewed as a direct indicator that the divine decree for the final upheaval is imminent.
